🗓 **TAWG Daily Catch-up**
_2026-09-25 23:00 → 2026-09-26 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **Subject-binding gap confirmed with a 6-case witness** — Baby Blue Viper linked the Agent Manifest v0.2 composition hole to a runnable checker; all six cases passed. [tg:tawg:4936]

> **Research-to-gap relay closes the loop** — Pavlo's Data Passports reference fed Baby Blue Viper's gap analysis, which Pavlo then verified upstream against the pinned spec and current main. [tg:tawg:4951]

> **On-chain domain() verified against ERC-7812 and Sourcify** — the full struct layout and admin address were confirmed, giving the group a grounded on-chain baseline. [tg:tawg:4947]

## 🤝 **What moved**

### subject-binding

_Analysis and witness work on the Agent Manifest subject-binding gap moved from identification into confirmed reproducible evidence._

- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Shared** exact academic references for Data Passports, an ICLR 2026 submission on confidentially provable ML provenance, supplying the precedence framing that grounded the subject-binding discussion and connected ML research to the Agent Manifest gap. [tg:tawg:4933]

- Baby Blue Viper (@babyblueviper1) **Identified** the specific subject-binding hole in Agent Manifest v0.2 after reading both works, showing precisely where the composition remains uncovered and sharpening the group's shared picture of what needs to be fixed. [tg:tawg:4935]

- Baby Blue Viper (@babyblueviper1) **Shipped** a six-case conformance witness that runs with a single Python command, converting an abstract gap into a concrete reproducible test that reviewers can point to directly. [tg:tawg:4936]

- Baby Blue Viper (@babyblueviper1) **Refined** the rule-precedence fix on PR #55, noting that the initial commit keyed on kind alone and incorporating Zexo's and Pavlo's inputs so the correction is grounded in all three lines of analysis. [tg:tawg:4945]

- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Reviewed** commit 1c2f470 carefully against the pinned Agent Manifest spec, verifier, tests, and current main, independently confirming the subject-binding gap is real and still exists upstream — a detailed check that strengthens the group's case for acting. [tg:tawg:4951]

### ERC-7812

_On-chain and spec verification work moved the domain-struct question from open interpretation to confirmed, auditable fact._

- Zexo (@zexoverz) **Clarified** the full layout of the `domain()` struct and identified the leading address as the ERC-7812 Registrar, resolving an interpretation question and giving the group a precise shared vocabulary for follow-on work. [tg:tawg:4937]

- Baby Blue Viper (@babyblueviper1) **Verified** the admin address and full `domain()` return values on-chain and against Sourcify, confirming the EOA status of the admin and the complete struct, grounding any follow-up ERC-8301 work in auditable evidence. [tg:tawg:4947]

- Baby Blue Viper (@babyblueviper1) **Checked** the ERC-8301 text at the ethereum/ERCs head before responding on the sync question, then asked Zexo to open a sync PR following the pattern of PR #18, keeping spec and implementation aligned. [tg:tawg:4946]

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**

- Explore whether the Data Passports composition approach from the ICLR 2026 submission can inform a concrete fix for the Agent Manifest subject-binding gap
- Discuss the upstream implications of the subject-binding gap remaining in current main

### ✅ **TODOs**

- Zexo to open the ERC-8301 sync PR following the pattern of PR #18
- Follow up on the tightening suggestions Pavlo noted while reviewing 1c2f470 against the pinned spec

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** A research reference arrived early in the window, a gap analysis and conformance witness followed hours later, and a careful upstream review closed the loop by evening — the same thread passed forward until it became a concrete, reproducible finding.
>
> When the relay runs that cleanly from reference to witness to upstream confirmation, even open gaps start to look like traction. Keep the chain moving! 🔗
